newsitem.title: USA: Union says Harrah's proposal gets backing.
newsitem.headline: Union says Harrah's proposal gets backing.

text.p: Hotel Employees & Restaurant Employees International Union said Friday that a "substantial" majority of shareholders voted against Harrah's Entertainment Inc's poison pill.

The union said that preliminary results show a majority of votes cast approved a proposal to amend the by-laws of Harrah's Entertainment Inc to redeem the company's poison pill and require prior approval by a majority shareholder vote for adoption of any such poison pill in the future.
However, according to the union, Harrah's says its certificate of incorporation requires a 75 percent supermajority vote for shareholders to amend the bylaws.
"We feel that the 75 percent vote requirement is an illegal restriction on shareholders' statutory powers to amend the bylaws," the union said in a press release.
A union spokesman said he did not have the vote count yet because the figures were still being tallied.
He said that the issue may have to be settled through litigation.
